newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Tajik opposition leader arrives in Afghan city.
newsitem.headline: Tajik opposition leader arrives in Afghan city.

text.p: Tajik opposition leaader Sayid Abdullo Nuri on Monday arrived in the Afghan town of Kundez for peace talks after his aircraft was delayed by Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia, the United Nations said.

U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said Nuri and his delegation had landed in Kunduz, in northern Afghanistan. The talks were expected to begin once Tajikistan's President Imamali Rakhmonov and the U.N. special envoy, Gerd Merrem, arrived in Kunduz.

Nuri was travelling in a U.N. aircraft on Saturday to the talks when jets of Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia forced it to land. The Taleban said on Sunday the plane had been released and authorised to continue its flight.

Foa said there apparently was a misunderstanding between the United Nations and the Taleban, who should have given clearance for the flight. Instead it was first diverted to Shindan near Herst in southeast Afghanistan and then to Kandahar.
Fighting has flared in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan since the talks were announced at the end of last month as each side moves to strengthen its hand at the negotiating table.
There have also been a spate of attacks against Russian servicemen based in Tajikistan, who help prop up Rakhmonov's administration. The opposition is widely held to have been responsible.

Tens of thousands have been killed and many more made homeless in the bitter four-year civil war in the mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China. Regional and clan rivalries underlie the conflict between the Islamist rebels and the secular government.
